title: Beyond the Building — An Arcade Geography
text:
FIELD NOTES / A PERSONAL RESEARCH PROJECTA conventiondoesn’t endat the door.Games, people, machines and ideas converge for a weekend. Their connections reach beyond the exhibition hall.Follow the story ↓SEATTLE · PORTLAND · BEYONDA RESEARCH PROJECT IN PROGRESS01 / PAX WEST, 2018Photograph: project authorThe event was visiblebefore I reached the building.

THE QUESTION THAT STARTED ITHow far does an event extend—and what happens before and after the doors open?Walking toward a convention in Seattle, I noticed activity before reaching the venue. That observation became a spatial question, then a network question: what gathers here, what happens nearby, and what carries on elsewhere?

CHAPTER 01 / THE IDEAA “bomb chart”with more than one center.An informal research model for an event’s geographic reach. Begin with an anchor, then look for surrounding activity and the relationships connecting it.ReachEcosystemStart with a geographic question.An illustrative ring asks what might be observed around the venue. It is a way to frame investigation, not a measured boundary of impact.Illustrative distance 500 mChange the scale to explore the idea. No radius here represents a measured economic or causal effect. Convention anchor Surrounding activityINDIE SHOWCASEHOTEL EVENTLOCAL ARCADEMEETUPCONVENTIONCONCEPTUAL DIAGRAM · NOT A STREET MAPFROM RADIUS TO RELATIONSHIPSA hotel activation, indie showcase or arcade meetup can become another center of activity. Proximity helps describe the pattern; source evidence tells us how an event relates to the convention.

CHAPTER 04 / A PERMANENT SCENE TAKES SHAPEBremerton.One scene, several forms of play.I follow documented openings from a family arcade to a barcade, a board-game and pinball pub, a VR space and a pinball-focused venue. I name the businesses, while omitting the people involved. This schematic map separates documented openings from neighboring cultural activity and undated research leads.Documented through 20151 documented openingWATERFRONT CONTEXTSCHEMATIC DISTRICT · NOT VENUE COORDINATESPositions illustrate the wider scene, not addresses or distances. Green nodes are documented arcade openings; rust nodes are surrounding context. An undated bookshop lead is shown in gray. Historical appearance does not establish continuous operation.Evidence: workbook “Bremerton Diffusion” and “R Cluster Timeline,” drawing on contemporary local reporting and a 2024 retrospective. Business names are retained; personal names are omitted. Current context, reopenings and undated leads are distinct from the five documented arcade openings.AN OPEN HISTORICAL LEADI remember Another Castle as part of this scene. A 2024 local retrospective reports that it was taken over and reopened as Town Portal. I show this as a change in name and operation, preserving the historical venue rather than assuming that activity vanished.CHAPTER 05 / THROUGH TIMEGrowth leaves a record.The record has gaps.Explore selected historical measurements from the workbook. CHAPTER 06 / DIFFERENT EVENTS, DIFFERENT FLOWSThe same questions.Different ecosystems.A collector convention, an indie showcase and a trade show gather different people and equipment.
